chose: drop recipe_pending_image.source_url entirely and make object_key NOT NULL
over: keeping source_url as provenance-only with a rule that read paths must never use it
leaving the URL-only fallback row for hotlink-blocked hosts
because: the column is the only thing that makes 'we stored the original image URL' representable; a rule not to read it is a rule that drifts, and the read path had already drifted (household-recipes.ts served it straight to the browser). Page provenance still lives in recipe_attribution.url.

chose: browser fetches/reads image bytes and PUTs them to a staged bucket key before commit; server-side SSRF-guarded fetch is the fallback
over: browser-only upload with no server fallback
because: the server is hotlink-blocked or paywalled on many recipe hosts while the browser carries the user's own referer/cookies and, for folder imports, already holds the File bytes. Neither alone covers the corpus: browser fetch dies on CORS-less CDNs, server fetch dies on hotlink blocks.

chose: an S3 PUT of an object key containing ':' fails AccessDenied against local-s3, while the same PUT with the colons stripped succeeds
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes

SigV4 canonical-URI mismatch: the AWS SDK and local-s3 disagree on whether ':' (and '%') is percent-encoded when building the string to sign, so the signature never matches and the server reports it as AccessDenied rather than SignatureDoesNotMatch
discriminatedBy: probe four keys through the same client and credentials, varying only the charset: staged/did:plc:abc/01ABC, staged/didplcabc/01ABC, staged/did%3Aplc/01ABC, plain/key

chose: SigV4 canonical-URI mismatch on ':' and '%' in the object key
because: The probe isolated the charset: identical client, credentials, bucket and body; only the key differed. 'staged/didplcabc/01ABC' and 'plain/key' both round-tripped, while 'staged/did:plc:abc/01ABC' and 'staged/did%3Aplc/01ABC' both failed AccessDenied. That rules out the instrument (same client, two of four keys passed) and rules out permissions (the account has full access to the bucket) — what is left is the signing canonicalization of ':' and '%'.

chose: partition staged uploads by SHA-256 of the DID rather than the DID itself
over: the raw DID in the object key
because: a ':' in an S3 object key fails the SigV4 signature check against local-s3 and reports as AccessDenied; '%' fails identically so escaping is not a fix (probe: four keys, one client — only the ':' and '%' ones failed). Hashing also keeps user identifiers out of a bucket listing, so two reasons and either would carry it alone.

chose: add local-s3 to the dev stack; local dev no longer touches the shared Railway bucket
over: keeping BLOB_S3_* pointed at the remote buttery-uploads bucket (the 2026-08-12 decision)
because: the image path is now the whole image path rather than a narrow pre-publish feature, so a laptop that cannot reach a bucket cannot exercise it at all — and the one part of local dev that talked to Railway was also the one where a local mistake wrote objects other developers see. local-s3 over MinIO: one binary, one env var, bucket created by an API call on boot, no cluster or IAM. Cost is path-style-only routing, hence BLOB_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE.
